seal.statement: The partition CDC obligation lane ships every owed obligation after its scan cursor, up to the existing count bound and a byte bound, as one ordered vector in one durable wave: draining a backlog of B owed rows takes at most ceil(B / bound) waves plus one per byte-bound split instead of B waves, while order within the partition, exact occurrence identity, the acknowledgement rule (a row is delivered only by a committed CDC_DELIVERED proposed after every current leaf returned a committed receipt for a vector containing it) and the idempotent recipient effect are unchanged.

Transition record and scope before any edit (contract-first checklist; base 9a22bf79b, rule-set revision 5; lead = takeover session 2026-11-14, writer = one implementation subagent, verifier = separate subagent). Design source: cdc-delivery-design-note-2026-11-11.md section 4 (Stage 1) on wip/formation-integration-20261111, direction endorsed by external review; its Stage 2/3 code is NOT imported (last verdict on that code REJECT, no physical proof). Cause measured on ed708dfd: see evidence/receipt.json. History: slot introduced 2026-10-23 (681da1dc1) as a memory/custody bound, lane page read reduced 256 -> 1 the same day to stop preloading payloads across awaits; batching on the durable path was never decided against; 15 slicing patches 10-27..11-08 tuned around the slot without measuring sender latency. Comparable systems (etcd/raft MsgApp batching and inflights, TiKV per-connection batching, Kafka fetch batching, PostgreSQL walsender) all batch per ordered stream and acknowledge by position.
1 Producer/consumer symbols: producer driveCdcObligations -> driveOnce -> drivePage/deliverObligation (becomes one vector per await) in src/partition/partition-cdc-obligation-delivery.js; progress cell in partition-cdc-obligation-progress.js; subscriber wrapper deliverCDCEventToSubscriber/buildCDCSubscriberWrapper in partition-cdc-delivery.js; buildPartitionCdcPropagationSubscriber; propagatePartitionCDCEvent (seed-runtime-bridge-owner, node-joining-publication-activation and their delegates); CDCGroupPropagationService.propagateCDCEvent/assertPropagationRequest -> propagateDurableCdcEvent (captureCdcEvents(options.events)); unchanged consumers source.applyCDCBatch / messageRouter.deliver -> applyDurableCdcBatch; the second durable subscriber (live-query, subscribeToCDCWithHandshake) takes the same vector contract.
2 Owner-defined shape: the vector is the existing frozen event array of captureCdcEvents, each member eventOf(obligation); the answer is the existing committed/provisional/unknown outcome over that vector; no new type.
3 Identity/generation: event (sourcePartition,eventKey,digest); vector cdcVectorDigest; lane leadership tenure; subscriber subscriptionEpoch; recipient groupId + observed route lifetime; receipt (groupId,logIndex,term). Unchanged; only the vector length differs.
4 Ordering: rows read ORDER BY log_index, ordinal; the vector preserves it; the recipient commits one entry and applies members in array order; vectors of one partition are sent one at a time (lane single-flight), so vector order is log order. No ordering claim across partitions (architecture: delivery has no global ordering).
5 Absent vs unavailable: no owed rows DRAINED; no subscribers NO_SUBSCRIBERS; recipient not committed cdc_committed_acceptance_unknown with deferRetry; not leader NOT_LEADER. Unchanged typed outcomes.
6 Durable commit: unchanged. Recipient group commit of the CDC batch makes the receipt; the source partition's commit of CDC_DELIVERED makes rows delivered.
7 Retained obligations: every row of an uncovered vector stays owed; a partially covered vector keeps covered leaves in the pinned cell (positions and digests only) and the retry presents the same vector; if the pinned range no longer reads back identically (rows acknowledged through hydration) the cell is discarded and rebuilt, re-delivery being idempotent; hydrated-prefix rows are acknowledged per row before any await exactly as today.
8 Wake/cleanup: unchanged wakes (committed entry, leader elected, handshake, retry timer, after flush); lane reset on tenure change discards the cell.
Writable paths: src/partition/partition-cdc-obligation-{constants,delivery,progress,lane}.js, src/partition/partition-cdc-delivery.js, src/bootstrap/shared/partition-cdc-propagation-subscriber.js, the propagatePartitionCDCEvent pass-throughs under src/bootstrap/**, src/topology/cdc-group-propagation-{service,durable-delivery}.js (request shape only), the live-query durable subscriber adapter under src/live-query/**, and the tests that pin the one-event call shape (design note 4.7) plus new reproducers R1-1..R1-5 (4.8). Excluded: ledger, CDC_DELIVERED, message-group files, cache, slot/slicing behaviour, recipient cursors, re-list, the partial-row cache writer, any timeout/bound value. Open counterexamples to witness: a vector containing several versions of one key applies in order (R1/O12); a hydrated prefix inside a page; an oversized single row; partial coverage then retry with identical digest; acknowledgement backpressure on the first row; a subscriber that is not the propagation subscriber.

SUPERSESSION RECORD (R09) and final coverage model, 2026-11-14, by the lead after Phase A (reproducers red on the sealed base: lab jobs 456812e5 adams-gamla and e94b128b tv-dator at 6f446edf9) and two read-only model challenges retained at lagrange-foundation-coordination-20261114/range-shipping/challenge-state-events.md (A1-A15, B1-B7) and challenge-timing-interleaving.md (M-1..M-13). The sealed text is not edited; where this record differs from the sealed statement or constraints, this record governs and the verifier is briefed with it. Authority: owner 2026-11-11 (supersede sealed decisions where provable stability needs it); nothing here weakens acceptance.

S-1 supersedes the statement clause 'at most ceil(B / bound) waves plus one per byte-bound split'. It was false in two ways: rows already pending acknowledgement leave holes that split a run (A3, M-10), and a fixed full vector is weaker than one row per wave under faults: one member that can never be applied blocks the rows ahead of it (A1) and a vector whose commit never fits the recipient's attempt budget never moves (A6, M-1). Replacement claim: every wave ships the maximal run of consecutive READY rows after the cursor, cut only by the lane's current window, the byte bound, an acknowledgement or retained-delivered bound, and whole-entry boundaries; the window is a row count in [1, ACK_BATCH_MAX_EVENTS] owned by the lane tenure, starting at 1, doubling after each vector that reached committed coverage while it was cut by the window (more READY rows were available) and halving (floor 1) after each vector that was admitted, attempted and left uncovered; a refusal that attempted nothing (typed backpressure: slot busy, owner not ready, acknowledgement backpressure) and provisional coverage leave it unchanged. With window 1 the lane ships one whole entry per wave, which is the sealed base's behaviour with the READY ordinals of one entry travelling together (an incoming row of equal version is accepted by the cache merge, so a cut between same-entry siblings that later moves could regress a covered recipient); under any fault the lane therefore delivers at least what one entry per wave delivers; without faults a backlog of B rows drains in at most ceil(B / bound) + log2(bound) waves plus one per byte split and per hole. This is the congestion rule of comparable systems (etcd probe/replicate, Kafka dropping to one in-flight after a failure, TCP slow start); it is one path with one parameter, not a second path.
S-2 supersedes constraint scheduling-bound-not-payload-cap, sentence 'derived from limits their owners already state ... imported from those owners'. No owner states such a limit: the router sets no maxPayload (ws default 100 MiB, exceeding it closes the peer connection), the message-group proposal codec and CDC_BATCH have no size check, raft-rs max_size_per_msg 1 MiB is a soft batching limit and entries travel base64 (x1.33). Replacement: SHIP_MAX_BYTES is a lane-owned scheduling bound in PARTITION_CDC_OBLIGATION_BOUND, 256 KiB of summed event_json, derived from those facts and the 1500 ms per-attempt propose timeout; SHIP_MAX_EVENTS is ACK_BATCH_MAX_EVENTS. Both remain scheduling bounds: the unit of shipping is a ledger entry (the READY ordinals of one log_index are never cut apart), a vector always holds at least one entry, and an entry above either bound ships alone and whole; nothing is refused, split or dropped. The synchronous apply span of a full vector at a recipient is measured on a lab host and recorded before acceptance (M-3).
S-3 supersedes constraint one-contract-no-adapter, sentence 'The non-durable user-table path is untouched', and constraint memory-and-custody-unchanged where they conflict with one contract. The subscriber wrapper and raw subscribers are shared by the durable lane and the non-durable producer (generateCDCEvent, buffered replay). Replacement: there is exactly one subscriber contract, (events, deliveryContext) with events a dense ordered vector of one table and one partition; every producer uses it and the non-durable producer passes a vector of one with unchanged behaviour. No per-event entry point survives.
S-4 scope amendments (R16), all inside the same interaction: (a) src/partition/partition-cdc-obligation-ledger.js gains read-only range queries (positions, entry ids and payload byte lengths without payloads; payloads for a chosen range) because reading up to 256 full payloads before applying the byte bound is unbounded memory (A10); no schema or write change. (b) src/bootstrap/phases/seed-cache-hydration-cdc-subscription.js and the replica-registration hook site: beforePropagation takes the vector; the seed NODES node-ready trigger walks members in order and uses the previous member of the same node inside the vector, else the cached row, as its previous row; afterPropagation runs once per vector (A5). (c) the non-durable producer call sites and the live-query handler adopt the vector contract (S-3). (d) every test and fixture that pins the one-event call shape (about 37 files). Still excluded: message-group files, cache, slot and slicing behaviour, any timeout, hold, retry count or cooldown value.

DESIGN DECISIONS for the candidate: 1 Composition is fresh at every drive step from the ledger: metadata read, per-row pre-pass exactly as the base (pending skip, hydrated acknowledgement, acknowledgement backpressure, READY) with the retained-delivered bound applied cumulatively over the rows being added (A2, M-5), then the cut, then a payload read of the chosen range only; no SQLite read across an await and no payload retained between attempts. 2 Pinning: while the current progress cell holds any leaf coverage the next composition is capped at the cell's last position so the identical vector (same digest) is presented and covered leaves are not re-sent; the cell is discarded and rebuilt when the window fell below its row count or its rows no longer read back identically (hydration, acknowledgement) (M-8, M-9). 3 Acknowledgement after committed coverage is per row in order; if acknowledgeDelivered refuses at row k the cursor stops before row k, the rows from k stay owed and the drive outcome says so (M-4). 4 retireHydratedInvocationAndResetIdleScan retires an in-flight vector only when its last position is at or below the hydrated index. 5 Per-member effects keep per-member order and count: CDC_EVENT emits, EVENTS_DELIVERED, sequence numbers, table guard for every member (single-table invariant asserted, B1). 6 Slot admission and slice bookkeeping read the vector's table; their behaviour is unchanged.

FINAL COVERAGE MODEL (replaces the draft). Claim: for a fixed ledger content and a fault schedule keyed by row identity (not by call number), (i) each recipient's committed command log, flattened, contains every owed occurrence (eventKey) at least once, each unchanged, and its first occurrences are in (log_index, ordinal) order; (ii) every row is eventually delivered and none is named by a CDC_DELIVERED before every current leaf of every current subscriber holds a committed receipt for a vector containing it; (iii) nothing is dropped, refused, split inside an entry, merged or reordered by the sender; (iv) with the window forced to 1 the lane's externally relevant result equals the sealed base's at entry granularity; (v) the wave bound of S-1. Decisions: composition, pre-pass, cut, pin or rebuild, window update, acknowledgement, cursor, outcome, retry scheduling. State: owed rows 0/1/below/at/above bound/above DRIVE_PAGE_ROWS; sizes small/oversized entry at head, middle/cumulative crossing; entries with several ordinals at a cut; several versions of one key; INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE; hydrated index none/prefix/inside the vector/whole/moving; pending rows at head/middle/tail; acknowledgement batch and outstanding commands at each bound, held lane, retained-delivered near its bound for head and non-head rows; subscribers none/propagation/propagation plus a second durable subscriber/foreign table; leaves source only/one/several targets/target without route/recipient set growing; slot free/busy; window 1/intermediate/at bound; one-row versus multi-row vectors (different wire and command types, A4). Events: answer committed/provisional/unknown/backpressure with hint/throw/never settles; a member that can never be applied (poison) at head/middle/tail; partial coverage across leaves and across subscribers, then success; route replaced; hydration handshake during flight and while pinned; new rows committed during flight; CDC_DELIVERED committed/refused terminal and non-terminal/unknown/proposer unavailable/identity compacted; tenure, subscription epoch or propagation lifetime change; shutdown; drive requested while one runs; identical vector re-presented while its wait is open; a rebuilt overlapping vector while an older one may still commit (M-7, A7). Temporal: before the read; between metadata read and payload read; before the first await; while awaited; between attempts; after coverage before acknowledgement; between acknowledgement and its commit; after the step with child operations still open (M-11); after the pass. Outputs: recipient command logs and digests; CDC_DELIVERED proposals; owed rows; drive and flush outcomes; window value; retry disposition and delay values; emits, metrics, sequence numbers; what the lane retains between attempts. Evidence: differential window=1 versus windowed over generated ledgers and row-keyed fault schedules; literal anchors built from raw ledger event_json (never through eventOf or captureCdcEvents) and read from the recipient's committed command log (never only the cache); the Phase A reproducers; enumerations imported from their owners; mutation by mechanism with a guard-versus-mutation table (vector reordered; row dropped at a cut; entry split; covered leaf re-sent with a changed digest when nothing changed; row acknowledged before the last receipt; hydrated row delivered; pending row re-delivered; cursor advanced past an unacknowledged row; window not halved after an attempted failure; window halved on backpressure; window not restored by success; payload retained between attempts; read held across an await; retained-delivered bound not cumulative; oversized entry refused or split; a bound or delay value changed).
FINDINGS ROUTED, NOT ABSORBED (R17): the recipient handler deduplicates by table:operation:key:timestamp, so same-entry same-key siblings can lose a member today, independent of batching (belongs to the same-entry ordering unit); one-row and multi-row vectors use different wire and command types (unify later); the live-query handler returns no receipt and would hold a lane on a partition that records obligations; a lane refused by the node-wide slot has already materialised its vector, so refusal retries cost CPU in proportion to vector bytes until the slot unit removes the slot (M-2), and slot fairness counts waves not rows (M-6): both are measured on the journey and are the reason the slot unit follows immediately; the seed node-ready trigger is an edge trigger on a cache row that authoritative reconciliation can update first.
